newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS-Maine nuke plant to close after failed sale.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Maine nuke plant to close after failed sale.

text.p: A third New England nuclear power plant faced a premature permanent shutdown Friday after talks to sell the troubled Maine Yankee facility fell apart, officials said.

Philadelphia-based Peco Energy dropped its bid to buy the plant in Wiscasset because of economic concerns, and Maine Yankee's owners will begin the process of decommissioning the 25-year-old facility.

Maine Yankee President David Flanagan said they could not reach an agreement that was suitable for Peco and "at the same time had a benefit to Maine Yankee that was greater than the cost of shutting it down."

Maine Yankee was once considered one of the most efficient nuclear plants in the United States, but has been plagued for the past three years by equipment problems and allegations officials have fraudulently understated safety concerns.

The facility has been off-line since December after engineers found cables in a key safety system were misrouted. Repair efforts were largely suspended in May while its utility owners looked for a buyer.

"The owners concluded that without a sale to Peco they could not afford to repair and operate the facility on their own," said David Flanagan, chairman of Central Maine Power, which owns the largest share of the plant.
Taking apart and disposing of Maine Yankee will take 10 years and cost at least $370 million. It is expected to be the largest decomissioning project ever undertaken in the U.S. nuclear industry.

Maine Yankee will join Connecticut Yankee and Yankee Rowe in Massachusetts as the third New England facility to be shut down by its owners before its operating license expires. Maine Yankee was licensed until 2008.

Peco spokesman Bill Jones said despite the failure of these talks his company would continue to look at buying other nuclear plants. "That is one of our business strategies for the future competition and deregulation," Jones said.

Anti-nuclear activists, who held three unsucessful referendums to shut down the plant, praised Friday's news. "It is a relief for me not to fear for the safety of my family," said Chris Christine, a Wiscasset-area resident.
Maine Yankee is 38 percent owned by Central Maine Power Co. , 20 percent each by New England Electric System and Northeast Utilities, and 22 percent by other New England utilities.
